title: Learning: Used Once
text: A valid proof is just data. Unless it is tied to this verifier and this moment, anyone who has seen one can send it again.
held: The proof answered this request, and would be useless anywhere else.

cards.label: Send a fresh nonce and your own name for the proof to include
Accept any valid proof of the statement
cards.why: Then last week's proof, copied, is as good as today's. Whoever holds a copy becomes the prover.

cards.label: Make the proof for this nonce and this verifier
Send the proof you made for the cinema last week
cards.why: That proof was for another verifier and another moment. If the shop accepts it, so would anyone you ever showed it to.

cards.label: Reject the proof
cards.why: Nothing was wrong with it. Refusing something legitimate without looking is its own failure: check, then act.

fields.label: bound to
fields.check: Check what the proof is bound to
fields.ok: Made for your nonce, addressed to you.

intrusion.detail: The proof was made for a different verifier, days ago.
intrusion.why: A copied proof. It was true when it was made, for the person who made it; it says nothing about who is sending it now.
intrusion.reveal: The proof had been made for a different verifier a week earlier and replayed.

teaches: A proof must include something fresh from this verifier, or it can be replayed.
Naming the verifier inside the proof stops one verifier reusing it at another.
